gloss: Words and heart are not in agreement; to say one thing while meaning another.
teaser: Ever met someone whose words don't match their true feelings? This idiom captures that essence.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever met someone whose words don't match their true feelings? This idiom captures that essence.[break 1s]The phrase is: 口是心非, kǒu shì xīn fēi.[break 0.5s]口 (kǒu) means 'mouth', [break 0.5s]是 (shì) means 'is', [break 0.5s]心 (xīn) means 'heart', [break 0.5s]非 (fēi) means 'not'.[break 1s]So together, 口是心非 literally means 'the mouth says, the heart does not'. Figuratively, it describes someone whose words contradict their true feelings.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]This idiom originates from ancient Chinese literature, where it was used to describe a person who speaks deceitfully. It highlights the discrepancy between one's spoken words and their true intentions. In a world where honesty is valued, this phrase serves as a reminder to be wary of those who may not express their true thoughts. [break 1.5s]Example 1: 他对我说他很高兴，口是心非。 [break 1s]He told me he was very happy, but his words are not sincere.[break 1s]Example 2: 有些人嘴上说支持你，口是心非。 [break 1s]Some people say they support you, but their hearts do not agree.[break 1s]Example 3: 她总是口是心非，让我很困惑。 [break 1s]She is always saying one thing but meaning another, which confuses me a lot.[break 1s]So remember, 口是心非 means words and heart are not in agreement. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
